requirements.general_guidance: Florida sugarcane is concentrated on the organic muck soils south of Lake Okeechobee, with some acreage on nearby sands. It is a multi-year crop: one planting is usually harvested for several seasons. Growers manage the water table to supply water and slow muck subsidence, and fertilizer needs on muck differ from sandy soils, so follow soil tests. A sugar mill within hauling distance is essential.

requirements.general_guidance: Peanuts do best on well-drained sandy or loamy sand soils in North Florida. Rotate with grasses such as bahiagrass or corn to limit diseases and nematodes, and avoid planting peanuts in the same field more than one year in three. Peanuts need calcium in the pegging zone, so soil-test and apply gypsum when calcium is low. Inoculate seed with rhizobia in fields without a recent peanut history.

fl_windows.label: Winter: plant late Sep-Oct, harvest Dec-Mar

requirements.general_guidance: Florida strawberries are planted as bare-root or plug transplants in October on plastic-mulched beds and picked from December to March, centered on the Plant City area. Overhead irrigation is used to establish transplants and to protect blooms and fruit on freezing nights. Picking is hand labor several times a week, so plan labor and market access early.

extension_links.title: Chapter 16. Strawberry Production

requirements.source_notes: UF/IFAS EDIS (Vegetable Production Handbook of Florida and agronomy guides). Temperature limits: FAO ECOCROP. Lower rainfall bound: median FAO-56 crop water need (Kc from UF/IFAS AE456 or FAO-56 x Hargreaves ETo) at the four demo farms; upper bound is an estimate. Hard pH limits are estimates. max_freeze_days 3 (weighted): crowns survive to about 20 F and flowers and fruit are protected with overhead irrigation from about 31 F (FAWN, UF/IFAS CV201, HS403); freeze events are typically 1-2 nights (SWFWMD). At Plant City only the worst 10-15% of seasons (e.g. 2010) exceed 3. Still to verify: protection nights per season, and North Florida suitability.
requirements.scale_note: Strawberries can be grown on small blocks, but beds, transplants, labor, cooling, and contracts are substantial fixed costs.

requirements.general_guidance: Florida fresh-market tomatoes are grown on raised beds with plastic mulch and drip or seepage irrigation, mostly in fall, winter and spring; summer heat and rain bring disease. Stake and tie plants, keep fertility steady through the drip line, and scout often for whiteflies and the viruses they carry. Expect high input and labor costs, so arrange a buyer before planting.

requirements.scale_note: Vegetable acreage can be smaller, but packing, labor, cooling, and buyer contracts still favor commercial blocks.

fl_windows.label: Winter (South FL): plant Dec-Jan, harvest Mar-Apr

requirements.general_guidance: Watermelons favor well-drained sandy soils and warm weather. Most Florida acreage is planted in late winter for May-June harvest, ahead of other states. Use raised beds with plastic mulch and drip irrigation, plan for pollinizer plants with seedless varieties, and rotate fields to reduce Fusarium wilt.
